rulings.restated: Input — How many days in 2025 was it used that way (by you, your family or another owner, or by anyone staying free or below a fair rent)?
rulings.model: The restated list leaves out 'Anyone under an agreement that lets you use some other unit'. It also leaves out the exceptions for family 'unless the unit is rented at a fair rental price to that person as his or her main home' and 'Do not count as personal use: Any day you spent working substantially full time repairing and maintaining the unit'. Each of these can change the count.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: finding; i1040se p. 4, Line 2: personal use includes 'Anyone under an agreement that lets you use some other unit' and 'Do not count as personal use: Any day you spent working substantially full time repairing and maintaining the unit ...; or Any days you used the unit as your main home before or after renting it ... for at least 12 consecutive months'. The question and its help (rental.personal_any: family renting at a fair rent as a main home is not personal use) leave out the excluded repair and main-home days and the swap arrangement, so a converted former home fails the home test or is divided on wrong days (BUG-0918).

rulings.restated: Input — How many days in 2025 was it used that way (by you, your family or another owner, or by anyone staying free, below a fair rent or under a home swap)? Leave out days spent mostly repairing it, and days it was your main home before or after renting it out (or trying to) for 12 months or more in a row, or for less if you then sold or traded it.
rulings.model: The restatement counts every day used by 'your family or another owner' with no exceptions. The IRS text excludes family use where 'the unit is rented at a fair rental price to that person as his or her main home', and owner use 'under a “shared equity” financing agreement'. It also says 'working substantially full time repairing and maintaining' where the restatement says 'mostly repairing'.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: finding; the question omits p527 p. 26's exceptions for a family member renting at a fair rent as a main home and for shared-equity use (BUG-0994)

rulings.restated: Input — How many days in 2025 was it used that way (by you, your family or another owner, or by anyone staying free, below a fair rent or under a home swap)? Leave out days spent mostly repairing it, and days it was your main home before or after renting it out (or trying to) for 12 months or more in a row.
rulings.model: The main-home exclusion requires 12 months or more in a row. The IRS also allows a shorter period: 'for at least 12 consecutive months (or for a period of less than 12 consecutive months at the end of which you sold or exchanged it)'. The restatement also does not except family members renting it at a fair price 'as his or her main home'.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: finding; i1040se p. 4, Line 2 excludes main-home days around a rental of 'at least 12 consecutive months (or for a period of less than 12 consecutive months at the end of which you sold or exchanged it)'; the question names only the 12-month case. A 2025 sale of a listed building already refuses at rprop.screen, so the gap is a shorter rental ended by a later sale or exchange: low (BUG-0772). The family point is representation: the question asks days 'used that way', the use defined at rental.personal_any, whose help says family renting at a fair rent as their main home is not personal use.

rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Used as a home and rented fewer than 15 days: not reported" = true → helper "Zero"] [helper "Used as a home and rented fewer than 15 days: not reported" = false → helper "Rents less total expenses"]
rulings.model: The two branches are correct. Zero is right when the unit is used as a home and rented fewer than 15 days ('do not report the rental income and do not deduct any rental expenses'), and otherwise line 3 rents less line 20 is right. However, the line 21 instructions say 'If you have amounts for which you are not at risk, use Form 6198 to determine the amount of your deductible loss. Enter that', and the form says 'If result is a (loss), see instructions to find out if you must file Form 6198'. No refusal covers a loss with amounts not at risk, so the program would enter the full loss where the IRS text calls for the Form 6198 amount.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040se p. 7, Line 21, "If you have amounts for which you are not at risk, use Form 6198 to determine the amount of your deductible loss". The case is refused: rental.not_at_risk (asked of a property with a loss) refuses with Form 6198 (at-risk limits). The two branches are right, as the reply says. Project stands.
